header: THE DURGAPUR AREAS CARD, seen through the lens of the Steel Plant: I show its township's PIN codes first, then the 43 wards of the Durgapur Municipal Corporation with the areas of each, then the two assembly seats and the police stations. Tab 1 "PIN codes": the 19 codes of the city (713201 to 713219), each with its post offices and the wards that use it, in ITS OWN COLOUR; the Steel Plant's own post offices are marked. Tab 2 "DMC wards": every ward, its seat, its PINs and its areas (in English), with a search. Tab 3 "Assembly seats": Durgapur Purba and Durgapur Paschim, the wards of each, and the three gram panchayats of Kanksa that Durgapur Purba adds. Tab 4 "Police stations": which areas are under which of the four stations the roll names (Durgapur, Coke Oven, Kanksa, New Township), with the station's address from the Commissionerate's site, and a search that tells which station an area is under. The colour of a PIN is the same on every tab, and I always write the PIN's number too: colour is never the only sign. I fetch nothing: the data is a reviewed file with its sources and date (data.ts, which also says how the English spellings were made).

behaviours: the card opens on the PIN codes, with three tabs
the Steel Plant lens is at the top: the plant's own PIN 713203 and the source of it
all 19 PIN codes of the city are drawn (713201 to 713219), then the two Kanksa codes
exactly three cards carry the DSP mark (713203, 713204, 713205) and the others do not
each PIN card has its own colour (the rail and the dot), the same colour the chips of other tabs use
the post offices are listed with their kind (HO, SO, BO), the head office Durgapur is there, and Durgapur RS says 'no delivery'
a PIN card names the wards that use it, as buttons (ward 29 for 713211)
there is a search box, and a line that says how many PIN codes there are
the sources, the date and the 'may be re-drawn' note are at the foot
the PIN tab opened with a PIN searched shows only that PIN
the wards tab draws all 43 wards, each with its seat, in the order 1 to 43
a collapsed ward shows a preview of its areas and a button with the number of areas
opened on 'ward 22': one ward, already open, its areas grouped under the PINs 713216, 713209 and 713205 with the English names
searching an area opens the wards that have it, with only the matching areas, and says 'found'
a search with no result says so, in words
the seat filter is a tab list with the seat colours, and the English-is-a-transliteration note is shown
the seats tab has the two seats, with their numbers 276 and 277 and their names in English only
each seat shows its wards as buttons: 16 for Purba (1-10, 23-28) and 27 for Paschim (11-22, 29-43), with the ranges written out
the three gram panchayats of Kanksa are under Durgapur Purba only
the Lok Sabha seat is named: No. 39 Bardhaman-Durgapur
the numbers of each seat's panel are drawn: wards, polling areas, PIN codes (Paschim 27 wards, 306 polling areas)
'pin code', 'durgapur pin code', 'pincode', 'post office' open the PIN tab
'pin 713203' opens the PIN tab with that PIN; a ward number from 1 to 43 opens that ward ('ward 1', 'ward 43')
'dmc wards', 'wards', 'ward' open the wards tab; the seats' words open the seats tab
a person's name is never taken for the card: 'purba', 'purba mitra', 'paschim' and 'durgapur' alone are not it
an ordinary sentence is not taken for it, nor a ward number out of range
readLang reads 'tab|search' and falls back to the PIN tab
no 'new Date(' (dates go through Luxon) and no fetch (the data is a file)
the card uses only the text sizes that have a rule in the search window's stylesheet (xs to 4xl and 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17, 28 px) and no fixed leading
a search for 'Bengal Ambuja' in the wards tab finds the Ambuja areas and writes 'also Bengal Ambuja' right after the word Ambuja, in a badge
a search with text has our one clear button (red on hover and focus), the browser's own cross is switched off, and an empty search has none
no area carries a question mark, in any tab
the PINs on a ward card are buttons that jump to the PIN's group (every group is marked data-pin-group), and the card has no button inside a button
the PINs on the three gram panchayat cards (4 + 2 + 1) are buttons that jump, and no button sits inside another

the card has four tabs, the fourth 'Police stations'; the police tab has the four stations in the order Durgapur, Coke Oven, Kanksa, New Township, each with its address and its page on the Commissionerate's site
each station says its wards, polling areas and areas (Durgapur 325 polling areas, Coke Oven 111, Kanksa 81, New Township 80); no Bengali and no question mark
a search opens the stations that have a match and lists only the matching areas under their station
'Bengal Ambuja' is found on the police tab too, with the badge, under one station
a ward with areas under three stations shows all three tags, each a button to the police tab, and a station label on every area; a ward with one station shows one tag and no label on its areas
'durgapur police station', 'thana', 'police stations' open the police tab; 'ward 22 police station' opens it on ward 22; the railway words still open the trains; 'police' alone is not this card
readLang reads the police tab
while searching, a station with no match is not drawn (ward 28 is under three stations, not four; nothing matching draws none)

each station card has its telephone numbers as links you can press (a landline and the Commissionerate's mobile; Kanksa only the mobile), whom it reports to, and its posts: five under Durgapur PS, one under New Township PS

the near-the-gate post is said: Waria, near the DSP Main Gate, under Durgapur PS; the posts without a station are listed apart, and the two stations of the whole subdivision (Women PS, Faridpur PS) with their numbers
an emergency line (112) and the four sources with what to know of each are on the tab, and the caution that a number can change
searching 'waria' shows both the post that matches (with its station) and the six areas called Waria, under Durgapur and Coke Oven stations
searching a post's name that no area has ('banbahal') shows the post, draws no station card, and says posts match
searching 'bengal ambuja' finds both the areas (under their station) and the City Centre post at Bengal Ambuja
the posts and numbers draw no question mark and no Bengali letters; only the allowed text sizes
while searching, a station's own list of posts is not repeated (the 'Posts that match' panel has them): searching 'waria' draws one post row in the panel and none inside the station cards
